site_tagline: One calm place for notes, lists and tasks. Made by Ákos Kappel.
home_meta_title: Oriel: notes, lists and tasks that work offline
home_meta_description: One calm place for notes, shopping lists and tasks. Opens instantly, works without a connection, and keeps a household on the same list. No account needed to start.
home_f1_text: Type a line and press Enter. “Groceries: milk, eggs, bread” becomes a list, and a pasted paragraph becomes a note.
home_f2_text: Everything is saved on your device first, so Oriel opens instantly in a basement shop, on a train or on a plane.
home_f3_text: Invite family or friends to a space. Checked items show up on every phone moments later, with who checked them.
home_f4_text: Markdown notes, lists you reorder and reuse, and tasks with priorities, statuses and due days.
home_f5_text: Search everything, even offline. Ctrl+K jumps to any item or command, and j and k move through the list.
home_f6_text: No account needed, no ads and no trackers. Export everything to JSON or Markdown whenever you like.
home_s1_text: Notes live in a database inside your browser. Nothing waits for a server, and nothing leaves the device until you create an account.
home_s2_text: With an account, changes travel to your other devices in the background. Offline edits are sent as soon as the connection is back.
home_s3_text: Owners invite people as editors or viewers. The server checks every change against those roles before anyone else sees it.

about_meta_description: Oriel keeps notes, lists and tasks on your device first, works offline, and syncs and shares them with the people you choose.
about_lead: Oriel is one calm place for notes, lists and tasks. Everything is saved on your device first, so it opens instantly and works without a connection. With an account it syncs between your devices, and shared spaces keep a household or a team on the same list as it changes.
about_w1: Quick capture: type a line and press Enter. A first line becomes the title, and “Groceries: milk, eggs, bread” becomes a list. On phones that support it, you can also dictate or scan a product’s barcode into a list.
about_w2: Notes in Markdown, shown formatted and edited as plain text, with earlier versions to restore.
about_w3: Lists to check off, reorder by dragging or with the keyboard, and reuse; entries from earlier lists are suggested as you type.
about_w4: Tasks with a priority, a status, a due day and a repeat, for anyone or for one member, with Today and Upcoming views.
about_w5: Pin, snooze until a day, archive, and a trash that keeps deleted things for 30 days, with Undo right after deleting, clearing or moving things.
about_w6: Search across titles, text and list entries, on the device and offline, and a command palette (Ctrl+K) on a keyboard.
about_w7: Shared spaces with invite links, and roles for who may edit and who may only look. You see who added and who checked something off, who else has a list open, and what changed recently.
about_w8: Optional notifications: a morning reminder of the day’s tasks, and what others add or check off.
about_w9: Installable as an app, in English, Hungarian and Slovak, in a light and a dark theme, with the list and the open item side by side on a wide screen.
about_w10: Export to JSON, Markdown or a calendar file at any time, and import JSON back.
about_d1: No account is needed. Without one, your notes never leave your device.
about_d2: With an account, your notes sync to a server I run myself. Each device receives only the spaces its user belongs to, and the server checks every change against your role before saving it.
about_d3: No ads, no tracking scripts, no third-party analytics. Cookies only keep you signed in and remember your language.
about_d4: Signing out removes your notes from the device. Deleting the account removes it, and the spaces only you use, from the server too.
about_built_text: Oriel is a study of local-first software: a SQLite database in the browser, kept in step with PostgreSQL by a sync service, with every permission checked on the server. It is built with TanStack Start, TanStack DB, PowerSync and Better Auth, and runs on a home server.

faq_lead: What people ask about Oriel. Something missing? Write to me and I will add it.

faq_q4: How do I install it like an app?
faq_a4_android: Android (Chrome): open the menu and choose “Add to home screen” or “Install app”.
faq_a4_ios: iPhone and iPad (Safari): tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”.
faq_a4_desktop: Computer (Chrome or Edge): use the install icon in the address bar.
faq_a5: With an account, create a shared space and invite people with a link (or by email). Each invite is for an editor, who can change things, or a viewer, who can only look. Each link works once and expires after 7 days. Your personal space is never shared.
faq_q6: What happens when two people change the same thing?
faq_a6: Each field keeps the latest change: if one person renames a list while another checks off an entry, both changes stay. If two people edit the same text at once, the one saved last wins.
faq_q7: Can I get my data out?
faq_a7: Yes. Settings exports everything on the device as JSON, which Oriel can import again, or as Markdown, which opens in any notes app.
faq_q8: What happens when I sign out or delete my account?
faq_a8: Signing out removes your notes from this device; they stay in your account. Deleting the account removes it, your personal space and every shared space only you use, on the server and on the device. A shared space others still use needs another owner first.
faq_a9: No. Oriel is a personal project without ads, and its code is open source.
faq_a10: Oriel is built for current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on phones and computers, and tested most in Chrome. Private or incognito windows may refuse to keep the local database.
faq_a11: English, Hungarian and Slovak. It follows your browser’s language, and you can change it in Settings or at the bottom of these pages. The privacy policy, terms and accessibility statement are in English.
